business_problem: LeadTable needed to redesign its schema and search architecture after growth in lead volume and inconsistent funnel data caused performance failures for enterprise recruiting customers.
solution_summary: LeadTable modernized its recruitment platform on MongoDB by rebuilding its schema around scalable indexing and search instead of trying to hide data inconsistency in the front end. The company captures candidate leads from providers such as Meta Lead Ads, Perspective, and Funnel Cockpit, each of which emits different field structures. As lead volumes surged, that flexibility turned into tech debt that made server-side pagination, statistics, and enterprise-scale search unreliable. Working with MongoDB Professional Services, LeadTable re-engineered the data model, standardized how funnel data becomes searchable, and moved to MongoDB Search on Atlas for broad lead and applicant retrieval. The new architecture can paginate large tables in under 200 milliseconds, keep around 5 million daily requests moving, and support international growth without the crashes that hit earlier production workloads. Atlas therefore became the governed search layer for a recruitment dashboard built around power users, compliance, and scale.

solution_components.name: MongoDB Atlas
solution_components.role: Hosts LeadTable's rebuilt recruitment data model and serves as the operational data platform behind the dashboard.

solution_components.name: MongoDB Search on Atlas
solution_components.role: Provides fast search across leads and applicant data with the indexing and pagination performance needed for enterprise users.

data_flow: Lead data from providers such as Meta Lead Ads, Perspective, and Funnel Cockpit is normalized into MongoDB Atlas, indexed with MongoDB Search on Atlas, and then surfaced through the LeadTable dashboard with fast pagination, filtering, sorting, and aggregate statistics for recruiters.
business_outcome: LeadTable achieved 95% faster global search, 70ms latency, 200ms pagination on 30,000+ lead tables, and enough headroom to handle around 5 million daily requests across 3.7 million leads.
